text:
leah: Quick heads-up: audit showed a tenant requested audit copies but console shows zero collected samples for their route. edge logs show sample_decision=1 and header X-RDW-CONSENT=opt-in present.
diego: Interesting. Are we honoring tenant-level consent before quota checks? I thought consent gating runs at collector.
norma: Consent check and sampling decision happen at edge: edge tags request with X-RDW-SAMPLED=true and X-RDW-CONSENT=[opt-in|opt-out]. downstream router applies inspect_quota and may drop bodies when quota exhausted. collector currently refuses payloads if consent!=opt-in. So path is: decision -> quota -> forward -> collector consent check -> accept/reject.
leah: Problem: tenant expects that if they opt-in we will keep at least tokenized/hashed audit traces even when quota blocks full payloads. Right now we drop everything if quota prevents forward, which makes it look like we never sampled.
infra-bot: note: playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/consent-and-sampling 
jared: Proposal: change ordering so collector enforces consent but router always forwards a minimal audit envelope when sample_decision=true and consent=opt-in. Envelope contains no PII: {sample_id, route, tenant_id, consent_state, redaction_version, envelope_hmac}. This avoids moving KMS to edge.
diego: I like minimal envelope. We should also add a metric sample_envelope_forwarded and sample_envelope_dropped with labels {tenant, route, reason}. Alert if envelope_dropped > 0 for >5m.
norma: Console UX: show per-tenant consent state (opt-in/opt-out/unknown) and a small timeline for envelope vs payload counts. Three columns: sampled_decisions | envelopes_forwarded | payloads_collected. Amber badge when envelopes_forwarded > payloads_collected.
leah: Legal ask: sometimes they need the scrubbed payload for investigation. Envelope won't be sufficient. We'll need a secure-forward path where edge can redact and forward scrubbed content even if quota would otherwise block. That requires key access and extra audit. 
jared: For secure-forward we could implement an edge-redact service that has a short-lived, tightly scoped key from KMS (use HSM-backed audit log). Edge requests a one-time redact token from control plane, uses it, then the control plane records that redact token issuance. This keeps KMS usage limited.
diego: Complexity: control plane must be highly available and low-latency. Edge will add a round-trip. Maybe limit secure-forward only to tenants with a paid compliance tier.
leah: Agreed. Short-term steps: 1) always forward envelope when sample_decision && consent=opt-in 2) create metrics/enforcement and console indicators 3) add admin toggle expedite_forward for tenant-level debug 4) start RFC for secure-forward for compliance tier.
infra-bot: task created T-10021: add_metric:sample_envelope_forwarded, sample_envelope_dropped; console_panel:consent_audit_view; admin_toggle:expedite_forward -> assignees [norma,diego,jared]
norma: Implementation note: envelope must include redaction_version so collector can claim redaction compatibility. Use HMAC(envelope) with service key to allow later verification without revealing fields.
jared: For labels on metrics include consent_state and redaction_version. Also include sampling_policy (static|dynamic) so we can filter false positives.
diego: Admin toggle config example: 
```json
{ "tenant": "globex", "route": "/v3/chat", "expedite_forward": true, "expires_at": 1710000000, "reason": "sre-incident-2026-03" }
```
leah: We'll need RBAC + audit trail for that toggle. Console UX should make it obvious it's operator-only.
infra-bot: RFC draft: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/5841-consent-envelopes-and-secure-forward (draft created)
leah: can we also show a tiny inline explanation on console hover: "envelope = minimal non-PII proof that a sampled decision occurred; payload = scrubbed sample which may contain PII". Should reduce confusion during oncall.
norma: Agree. Also add exporter to Slack alerts channel when envelope_drops spike for a tenant.
diego: One more: add retention tag on envelope hmacs so legal can request a list of sample_ids for a date range without getting PII. That supports lookup workflows without exposing content.
jared: Ok team. I'll pick up RFC, norma will own metrics + console panel, diego will do router changes to always forward envelope when consent=opt-in. leah will coordinate with legal for secure-forward requirements.
leah: thanks all. follow-up in RFC and T-10021. :thumbsup:
